Evaluation.description:
How a rule's check is judged by `lighthouse eval`. A policy, not a
meaning: changing it moves no meaning version.

precision.description: The precision a check must reach, from 0 to 1. Default: 0.9.

recall.description: The recall a check must reach, from 0 to 1; no target when absent.

EventsSpec.description:
The mapping of the lines of an agent's stdout to the events of a report.
Each expression sees `line`, the JSON value of one stdout line (a line
that is not JSON is skipped), and `tools`, the table below; the keys that
describe one event also see `item` when `each` is set. The functions are
those of the one CEL environment (its strings, lists, math and encoders
extensions, and the optional syntax `line.?name.orValue("")`, since the
lines of a harness are as free in shape as they come) and `commands(text)`,
which reads a shell command line.

each.description:
A list: one event for each of its elements, each seen as `item` by the
keys below, for a line that holds several calls (a shell command with
a pipe, a change of several files). Without it a line is one event. A
failure is no event.

path.description:
The file or directory the call is about, or a list of them for one
event each (a call without any is one event without a path); a path
inside the directory the agent ran in is made relative to it, and one
outside it is kept apart as `outside`. A failure is no path.

pattern.description: What a `search` looks for, or the glob of a `list`.

said.description:
A string: what the agent said in the line, for the notes of the fix
(its reply of what is fixed and what is left). Read from every line,
selected or not; the pieces are joined by line breaks, and the last
few kilobytes are kept. Without it an agent whose output is mapped
says nothing.

select.description:
A bool: whether the line holds tool calls. A line it is false or
fails for is skipped.

tool.description:
The tool of the call: `read`, `search`, `list`, `edit` or `run`,
usually `tools[line.<name of the harness's tool>]`. A call whose tool
is none of them, or that fails here (a harness tool the table lacks),
is not an event.

tools.description:
The harness's tool names, each with the tool it is: a table to look up
with `tools[name]` or `name in tools`, not one to search.

FixScope.description:
How far the change of a fix may go, which the verifier checks. Ordered
from the narrowest. One model for every type of fix: a fix by CEL, by a
command and by a model are held to it the same way.

oneOf.description:
Only inside the symbol of the finding (its extent): the symbol it is
about, else the innermost one around it, else a short file as a whole.

Only the file of the finding. What a fix by a command has when it
declares no scope.

The file of the finding and the files it reaches: a file may change
when it holds a reference site (a call, a use, an import) of a symbol
changed in a file that may change, transitively. A signature changes
with its callers, and a caller whose own signature changes, with its
callers. What a fix by CEL or by a model has when it declares no scope.

Any file the analysis indexes in the run's scope, for a change that
is not about references, such as the consistency of a doc and a spec.

context.description:
The most code, in tokens (four characters each), that the brief of one
run of an agent carries around the findings: the signatures of what
the code uses, its imports and, for the scope `files`, the places that
refer to what may change. The code of the findings is always given. When
the rest is over this, what is farthest from the findings is left out
first, and the brief says how many items were. Default: `4000`.

decisions.description:
The decisions a model may fix, as ids or globs over them (`*` within
one segment of an id): `["design/exported-doc", "testing/*"]`. Only a
decision with a check and no fix of its own (`cel`, `command`) is
fixed, and only by the agent `[models] agent` binds; binding a model
enables nothing by itself. Default: none.

scope.description:
The widest change a fix by a model may make, for every decision. A
decision that declares no `scope` has this one; one that declares a
`scope` is narrowed to it, never widened. Default: `files`.

unsafe.description:
Whether a fix that is not safe (one by a model among them) is written
when its result is verified, as `--unsafe-fixes` does for one run;
otherwise it is reported with its diff and left for a hand to apply.
A user's file may set it. `--no-unsafe-fixes` turns it off for a run.
Default: `false`.

verify.description:
Programs that must pass over the project with the fixes by models in
place, such as its tests: a command line, or a table with a `command`,
a `timeout` (default `10m`) and the rest of a program. They run once
per fix run, after its rounds, on a scratch copy of the project, and
only in a trusted project. A program that fails (its `output` is
`status` unless it says `lines`) withdraws every fix by a model of the
run to a preview.

GeneratedSpec.description: What a project says about generated code.

check.description:
`skip`: no decision checks generated code; `include`: every decision
does. Unset, each decision's own scope says. A rule's `generated`
setting wins over both.

files.description: Globs of project-relative paths that are generated code.

Level.description:
A level a project can set: a severity, or `off`, which only
configuration has.

Metadata.description:
Who a resource is. Identity is `name`; grouping is by label, never by
where the document is stored.

annotations.description: Free notes; never used to select.

uid.description:
Identity that outlives the name: a UUID v4 assigned once, never derived
from the name (Kubernetes `metadata.uid`). Renaming a resource keeps it.

ModelsSpec.description:
The `models` table of a project: its bindings and limits, and its own
providers.

agent.description:
The model (`<provider>/<model>`), or the route of several, that fixes
by changing files: a headless agent run as a `command` without a
`protocol`, in a scratch copy of the project. It makes the fixes of
the decisions `[fix] decisions` lists, unless a rule binds its own
`agent`. A request moves to the next model of a route when one fails.

budget.description:
Requests a run may send to models that cost something; the subjects
of the rest are left to review. Default: 200.

classification.description:
The model (`<provider>/<model>`), or the route of several, that judges
a decision no rule binds and no trained model is attached to. A request
moves to the next model of a route when one fails. When the route
abstains, the subject is left to agent review.

explore.description:
The share, from 0 to 1, of the subjects an attached model fails that are
sent on to the next layer as if it had abstained, so that labels keep
coming from where the model is surest. The same subjects every run.
Default: 0.05.

providers.description:
The providers the project defines, by name; a name that is built in
overrides it.

routing.description: Which model of a route a request starts at. Default: `ordered`.

Names.description:
One name or several, in the order written: the protocols a provider speaks
(each operation uses the one that covers it: classification `typesafe`,
else `openai`), or the models of a route.

Output.description:
What a program prints, which decides what its result is. A program has one
of two results: findings (`lines`, `sarif`, `status`) or changes (`files`,
`stdout`).

oneOf.description:
One finding per line of stdout; a leading `path:line[:col]: ` places it,
and a line that is only a path of the project places it at line 1 of
that file, with the decision's title as the message.
A SARIF 2.1.0 log: one finding per result.

One finding when the exit code is not in `success`, with the tail of
stderr or stdout as its message.
The files the program changed in its scratch copy of the project.
The new text of `{file}`, on stdout.

OverrideSpec.description: Rules for the files and languages that match.

files.description: Globs of project-relative paths; empty matches every path.

languages.description: Language ids; empty matches every language.

PluginEntry.description: A plugin in `plugins`: a bare id, or an id with where to find it.

PluginRefSpec.description:
A listed plugin. `path` (relative to the config directory) names the
plugin directory instead of searching the plugin locations; `timeout` is
the per-request limit for process plugins, such as `30s`.

ProgramSpec.description:
A program as a list of arguments (a program with only a `command`) or as
a table: the form where either is accepted, such as the programs of
`[fix] verify`.

constructorPrefixes.description:
The name prefixes that make a function a constructor in this
language, replacing what its provider declares. Every decision that
tells a constructor apart shares them.

testNaming.description:
The parts of the test naming convention this project replaces in this
language; the others stay what its provider declares.

ProjectSpec.description:
A project's configuration, and the shape of a shareable one: `extends`
names any project, the way an ESLint config extends a shareable config.
An extended project contributes its `extends`, `rules` and `overrides`.
Its `plugins` and `languages` belong to the project that is run.

extends.description:
Projects whose rules apply first, in order: the `recommended` and
`strict` projects of each pack (`core/recommended`), or any `Project`
document of the catalog.

fix.description: What fixes may do, and how fixes by models are checked beyond the rules.

generated.description:
Which files are generated code, beyond what the providers and
`.gitattributes` say, and whether it is checked.

languages.description:
Options per language id; `constructorPrefixes` is the host's, the rest
goes to the language's provider.

models.description: The models that judge the decisions rules cannot prove.

overrides.description: Rules that apply to some files or languages only, after `rules`.

plugins.description:
Plugins that provide rules and languages; a bare id searches the
plugin locations.

rules.description: Level and options per decision id.

sandbox.description: The sandbox the programs of the project run in.

sources.description: Embedded source rules. The host language is inferred by normal file routing.

ProviderSpec.description:
A provider of models as the project writes it, under
`[models.providers.<name>]`. A model is named `<provider>/<model>`.

A provider is reached by exactly one of `url` (HTTP), `command` (a stdio
process) and `plugin` (an rpc plugin); the only exception is a `protocol`
of `openai` or `typesafe` alone, which is HTTP at that protocol's own
service. Fields that belong to one reach are refused on the others.

body.description:
HTTP only: a JSON object merged shallowly into every request body, its
keys overriding the body's own (the OpenAI SDK's `extra_body`).

command.description:
The reach as a stdio process under the process contract of a program
(see `docs/programs.md`): no shell, its own process group, a time
limit, a cap on output, the one environment plus the declared `env`,
and the project's trust. `{model}` stands for the model part of the
reference. An answer that does not fit the protocol's shape is no
answer. Without a `protocol` the prompt is plain text on stdin and the
program serves `agent`: it runs in a scratch copy of the project and
changes the files there.

events.description:
`command` without a `protocol` only: how the JSON lines of the
agent's stdout become the tool events of the fix report, in CEL (see
`EventsSpec`). Without it the report holds no events of this agent.

headers.description:
HTTP only: headers sent with every request. A value may hold
`${NAME}`, the user's variable `NAME`, which is never written into a
note, a log or a cache key; a variable that is not set fails the
request, naming it. Default at a protocol's own service:
`Authorization: Bearer ${OPENAI_API_KEY}` (`${TYPESAFE_API_KEY}`).

options.description: `plugin` only: what the plugin is told besides the model.

plugin.description: The reach as a listed plugin that offers models.

pointer.description:
`command` with `protocol = "typesafe"` only: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to
the response inside the printed JSON (stdout is one JSON value), when
the program wraps it in an envelope.

protocol.description:
The protocol spoken at the reach: `openai` (Chat Completions, which
OpenRouter, Ollama, vLLM and LM Studio also speak) or `typesafe`
(System One), or a list of them in the order of preference. Required
for `url`. A `command` speaks `typesafe` (it serves classification),
or plain text without a `protocol` (it serves `agent`); a `plugin` must
not name one: its handshake says what it serves.

sandbox.description:
`command` only: what the program may reach besides the project's
`[sandbox]`. A provider whose `sandbox.network` lists a host is remote.

timeout.description:
How long one request may take, such as `90s`: a run of a `command`
(default 2m, 10m for `agent`) or an HTTP request of a `url` provider
(default 2m; reasoning models may need `10m`). A `plugin` provider has
none: a plugin is not told one.

url.description: The reach over HTTP: where requests go.

Routing.description: Which model of a route a request goes to first.

oneOf.description: The first model, then the others in the order written.

Each request starts at the next model, so load is spread; the others
follow in the order written, wrapping.

agent.description:
The agent, or the route of several, that fixes this decision by
editing files, before the project's `models.agent`. Findings bound to
different agents in one file are fixed by one run each.

classification.description:
The model, or the route of several, that judges this decision, before
the project's `models.classification`. When it abstains, the subject is
left to agent review.

evaluation.description: How `lighthouse eval` judges this rule's check.

generated.description:
Check generated code with this rule (`true`) or not (`false`),
whatever the decision's scope and the project's `generated.check` say.

options.description: The decision's options, as its own schema declares them.

safety.description:
The safety of every fix of this decision, applied last: `safe` writes
them with `--fix` (trust the agent here), `unsafe` previews them
until `--unsafe-fixes`. Where layers disagree, `unsafe` wins.

RuleSetting.description:
How a rule is written in a spec: `warn`, `off`, or
`{ level: warn, options: { max: 10 } }`.

Safety.description: How much a proposed fix may be trusted to keep the program's meaning.

oneOf.description:
Probably right but a judgment call: written only when the project allows
it or the run asks for unsafe fixes, else previewed.

Sandbox.description:
What a program may reach besides what the project's `[sandbox]` lets every
program reach: its lists are added to the project's.

network.description:
Hosts the program may reach, through the proxy of the run: a name, or
`*.suffix` for every host below it, either with `:port`.

write.description:
Places besides its own that it may write: paths below the project, or
below the home directory with `~/` in front. Never a secret.

SandboxSpec.description:
The `sandbox` table of a project: every program Lighthouse runs for it
(command checks, fixers, formatters, `[fix] verify`, agents and command
providers) runs under the OS sandbox. It reads everything but the secrets
of the user and the project, writes only its scratch place, and reaches no
network but the hosts listed here and in its provider.

enabled.description:
Whether programs run in the sandbox. Default: `true`. `false` is an
error unless the project is trusted (`lighthouse trust`), and every
run says that programs run with your full access.

network.description:
The hosts that command checks and `[fix] verify` commands may reach,
through the proxy of the run: a name, or `*.suffix` for every host
below it, either with `:port`. A provider lists its own. Default: none.

write.description:
The places besides their own that command checks and `[fix] verify`
commands may write: paths below the project, or below the home
directory with `~/` in front, such as `target` or `~/.cargo/registry`.
Never a secret. Default: none.

Sarif.description:
How a SARIF log is read, under SARIF's own names. A result must pass both
lists.

columns.description:
The unit the program counts columns in, when its log does not say or
says wrongly. Default: the log's `columnKind`, else `utf16CodeUnits`.

levels.description:
SARIF `level`s to keep: `error`, `warning`, `note` or `none`; a result
without a level is a `warning`. Default: every level.

rules.description:
Globs over the result's `ruleId`, such as `errcheck` or `govet:*`: `*`
is any run of characters inside one segment, segments being separated
by `/` or `::`, and `**` is any number of segments, as in module path
globs. Default: every rule.

SarifColumns.description:
The unit a SARIF log counts columns in (`columnKind`, plus the bytes that
tools such as golangci-lint count without saying so).

SourceLanguageSpec.description:
Analysis destination for a source rule. Exactly one of provider and from
is required; from reads the language of each candidate.

context.description: Optional provider-specific values and selector projections.

from.description:
Candidate-relative selector returning the name of the language of each
candidate, as a document writes it: one of the aliases a provider
declares, in any case. A candidate whose name is absent or unknown is
not analyzed; it is text.

provider.description: Fixed opaque key in the provider registry.

syntax.description: Optional interpretation owned by the selected provider.

SourceRuleSpec.description: A source selection analyzed through a registered provider.

select.description: One selector over the host provider's selectable tree.

Stdin.description: What a program is given on stdin.

TestNamingSpec.description: The parts of a language's test naming convention a project replaces.

ancestors.description:
The tests of a module that tests an ancestor module count for the
nested module too.

prefix.description: Prefix of an owner test's name.

snakeCase.description: Names are compared in snake case.

program.description:
A program as the files write it. Where a program is a table of its own
(a `check` or a `fix`), its fields stand beside the others.

command.description:
The program and its arguments, run without a shell. `{file}`,
`{files}`, `{line}`, `{symbol}`, `{decision}` and `{model}` fill whole
arguments where the binding point accepts them; they say how many
files a run is given. A decision's `check` and `fix` may leave it out
when each language it covers gives its own program under
`languages.<id>`.

env.description:
Variables the program is given besides the one allowlist. A value may
hold `${NAME}`, the user's variable `NAME`, which is never written
into a command line, a note, a log or a cache key; a variable that is
not set fails the run, naming it.

output.description:
What it prints, which decides the result. Default: `lines` for a
check, `files` for a fix, `status` for a `[fix] verify` program.

sandbox.description: What it may reach besides the project's `[sandbox]`.

sarif.description: How a SARIF log is read; only with `output: sarif`.

stdin.description: What it reads on stdin: nothing, or the text of `{file}`.

success.description:
The exit codes that mean the program ran; any other code, a signal or
a timeout is an error. Default: `[0, 1]` for `lines` and `sarif`
(linters exit 1 with findings), `[0]` otherwise.

timeout.description:
How long it may run, such as `30s` or `2m`. Default: `2m`; `10m` for
an agent and for a `[fix] verify` program.
